G5300.def: apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine"):--sow.

G5302.def: from «5306»; to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient):--come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse.

G5303.def: from «5302»; a deficit; specially, poverty:--that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want.

G5305.def: neuter of «5306» as adverb; more lately, i.e. eventually:--afterward, (at the) last (of all).

G5306.et: comparative from (5259) (in the sense of behind)
G5306.def: comparative from «5259» (in the sense of behind); later:--latter.

G5307.def: from huphaino to weave; woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted:--woven.

G5309.def: from a compound of «5308» and «5424»; to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant:--be highminded.

G5310.def: superlative from the base of «5311»; highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens:--most high, highest.

G5311.def: from a derivative of «5228»; elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity:--be exalted, height, (on) high.

G5312.def: from «5311»; to elevate (literally or figuratively):--exalt, lift up.

G5313.def: from «5312»; an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively):-- height, high thing.

G5315.et: a primary verb (used as an alternate of (2068) in certain tenses)
G5315.def: a primary verb (used as an alternate of «2068» in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively):--eat, meat.

G5316.def: prolongation for the base of «5457»; to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative):-- appear, seem, be seen, shine, × think.

G5317.def: of Hebrew origin («06389»); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch:--Phalec.

G5318.def: from «5316»; shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally:--abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly).

G5319.def: from «5318»; to render apparent (literally or figuratively):--appear, manifestly declare, (make) manifest (forth), shew (self).

G5320.def: adverb from «5318»; plainly, i.e. clearly or publicly:--evidently, openly.

G5321.def: from «5319»; exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment:--manifestation.

G5322.def: from «5316»; a lightener, i.e. light; lantern:--lantern.

G5323.def: of Hebrew origin («06439»); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite:--Phanuel.

G5324.def: from a derivative of «5316»; to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle):--sight.

G5325.def: from a derivative of «5324»; (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy"):--pomp.

G5326.def: from «5324»; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre:--spirit.

G5327.et: properly, strengthened from the base of (4008) or rather of (4486)
G5327.def: properly, strengthened from the base of «4008» or rather of «4486»; a gap or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent):--valley.

G5328.def: of foreign origin («06547»); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king:--Pharaoh.

G5329.def: of Hebrew origin («06557»); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite:--Phares.

G5330.def: of Hebrew origin (compare «06567»); a separatist, i.e. exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary:--Pharisee.

G5331.def: from «5332»; medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively):--sorcery, witchcraft.

G5332.et: from pharmakon (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion)
G5332.def: from pharmakon (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician:--sorcerer.

G5334.et: from (5346) (not the same as "phase", which is from (5316))
G5334.def: from «5346» (not the same as "phase", which is from «5316»); a saying, i.e. report:--tidings.

G5335.def: prolongation from the same as «5346»; to assert:--affirm, profess, say.

G5336.def: from pateomai (to eat); a crib (for fodder):--manager, stall.

G5337.def: apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked:--evil.

G5338.et: probably akin to the base of (5457) [cf (5350)]
G5338.def: probably akin to the base of «5457» (compare «5350»); brilliancy:--light.

G5339.def: of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently:--forbear, spare.

G5340.def: adverb from participle of «5339»; abstemiously, i.e. stingily:--sparingly.

G5341.et: by transposition for a derivative probably of (5316) (as showing outside the other garments)
G5341.def: by transposition for a derivative probably of «5316» (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout):-- cloke.

G5342.et: a primary verb (for which other and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only, namely, oio {oy'-o}; and enegko {en-eng'-ko)
G5342.def: a primary verb -- for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, oio oy'-o; and enegko en-eng'-ko to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows):--be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold.

G5343.def: apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish:--escape, flee (away).

G5344.def: of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman:--Felix.

G5346.et: properly, the same as the base of (5457) and (5316)
G5346.def: properly, the same as the base of «5457» and «5316»; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say:--affirm, say. Compare «3004».

G5347.def: of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman:--Festus.

G5348.def: apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at:--(already) attain, come, prevent.

G5350.et: probably akin to (5338) and thus to (5346)
G5350.def: probably akin to «5338» and thus to «5346»; to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim:--speak.

G5351.et: probably strengthened from phthio (to pine or waste)
G5351.def: probably strengthened from phthio (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave):--corrupt (self), defile, destroy.

G5352.pos:
1. autumn trees
    1. trees such as they are at the close of autumn, dry, leafless and without fruit
    2. metaph. of unfruitful, worthless men
G5352.def: from derivative of phthino (to wane; akin to the base of «5351») and «3703» (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves):--whose fruit withereth.

G5353.def: from «5350»; utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental):--sound.

G5355.et: probably akin to the base of (5351)
G5355.def: probably akin to the base of «5351»; ill-will (as detraction), i.e. jealousy (spite):--envy.

G5356.def: from «5351»; decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively):--corruption, destroy, perish.

G5357.def: of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial"):--vial.

G5358.def: from «5384» and «18»; fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue:--love of good men.

G5359.def: from Philadelphos (the same as «5361»), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor:--Philadelphia.

G5360.def: from «5361»; fraternal affection:--brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren.

G5361.def: from «5384» and «80»; fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal:--love as brethren.

G5362.def: from «5384» and «435»; fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife:--love their husbands.

G5363.def: from the same as «5364»; fondness of mankind, i.e. benevolence ("philanthropy"):--kindness, love towards man.

G5364.def: adverb from a compound of «5384» and «444»; fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely:--courteously.

G5366.def: from «5384» and «696»; fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious:--covetous.

G5367.def: from «5384» and «846»; fond of self, i.e. selfish:--lover of own self.

G5368.def: from «5384»; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while «25» is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as «2309» and «1014», or as «2372» and «3563» respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness):--kiss, love.

G5369.def: from «5384» and «2237»; fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous:--lover of pleasure.

G5372.def: from «5368»; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity:--Philetus.

G5374.def: from «5375»; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi:--Philippian.

G5375.def: plural of «5376»; Philippi, a place in Macedonia:--Philippi.

G5376.def: from «5384» and «2462»; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites:--Philip.

G5377.def: from «5384» and «2316»; fond of God, i.e. pious:--lover of God.

G5378.def: from «5384» and «3056»; fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian:--Philologus.

G5380.et: from (5384) and neikos (a quarrel, probably akin to (3534))
G5380.def: from «5384» and neikos (a quarrel; probably akin to «3534»); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious:--contentious.

G5382.def: from «5384» and «3581»; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable:--given to (lover of, use) hospitality.

G5383.def: from a compound of «5384» and «4413»; to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction:--love to have the preeminence.

G5384.def: properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.):--friend.

G5386.def: from «5384» and «4680»; fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher":--philosopher.

G5387.et: from (5384) and storge (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children)
G5387.def: from «5384» and storge (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian:--kindly affectioned.

G5388.def: from «5384» and «5043»; fond of one's children, i.e. maternal:--love their children.

G5389.et: middle voice from a compound of (5384) and (5092)
G5389.def: middle voice from a compound of «5384» and «5092»; to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something):--labour, strive, study.

G5390.def: adverb from «5391»; with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly:--courteously.

G5391.def: from «5384» and «5424»; friendly of mind, i.e. kind:--courteous.

G5393.et: active participle of the base of (5395)
G5393.def: active participle of the base of «5395»; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian:--Phlegon.

G5394.def: from «5395»; to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion):--set on fire.

G5395.def: from a primary phlego (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze:--flame(-ing).

G5396.def: from «5397»; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously:--prate against.

G5397.def: from phluo (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. prater:--tattler.

G5399.def: from «5401»; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere:--be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly), reverence.
